# Backend API capability inventory

The backend exposes no OpenAPI document. This inventory is based on the current Express routes, workflow schemas, agent implementations, and existing response types. The backend has no authentication middleware; the local demo login is not an access boundary.

metadata.title: Backend API capability inventory

documentation:docs%2Fapi-capability-inve.text:
[Backend API capability inventory]

mas, agent implementations, and existing response types. The backend has no authentication middleware; the local demo login is not an access boundary.

| Endpoint | Contract / behavior | Frontend use |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /health` | Status and database connectivity | Workspace connection indicator |
| `GET /api/company` | Company graph node | Workspace company name |
| `GET /api/graph` | Full graph nodes and edges | Dashboard metrics and organization graph |
| `GET /api/graph/neighborhood/:entityType/:entityId` | Direct neighbors and relationship direction, capped at 100 | Graph expansion; entity, ownership, decision, and impact views |
| `GET /api/search?q=` | Up to 50 graph records matching name, title, or email | Global search and assistant citations |
| `GET /api/employees[?departmentId&teamId&employmentStatus]` | Employee list/filter | People directory |
| `GET /api/employees/:employeeId` | Employee, manager, reports, department, team, skills, projects | People details and ownership/entity cards |
| `GET /api/departments[/:departmentId]` | Department list and department/team/employee details | Department directory/details |
| `GET /api/projects[/:projectId]` | Project list/details with owners, people, tasks, PRs, and services | Project directory/details and assistant cards |
| `GET /api/product-progress/graph` | Product Progress graph in the standard graph response shape | Product Progress graph |
| `POST /api/product-progress/tickets` | Validated ticket identification and graph persistence | Existing workflow capability; no automatic assistant write action |
| `POST /api/product-progress/activities` | Validated activity processing and graph persistence | Existing workflow capability; no automatic assistant write action |
| `POST /api/product-progress/workflow` | Routes ticket or feature update input | Existing workflow capability |
| `POST /api/assistant/query` | LangGraph retrieval and optional synthesis; validated structured answer with graph evidence and execution stages | Right-side assistant drawer and safe response renderer
| `GET /api/assistant/conversations` | Lists up to 50 conversations for the supplied workspace identity | Assistant conversation switcher
| `GET /api/assistant/conversations/:conversationId` | Returns persisted turns after checking conversation ownership | Restore a prior assistant conversation
| `POST /api/ingestion/process` | LangGraph validates source and limit, fetches normalized records, processes documents, and returns per-record outcomes | Integration settings "Fetch & process records" action |

metadata.title: Backend API capability inventory

documentation:docs%2Fapi-capability-inve.text:
## LangGraph ingestion behavior

The ingestion endpoint accepts `confluence`, `jira`, `github`, or `slack`, with an optional limit from 1 to 100. Confluence uses `CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL`, `CONFLUENCE_EMAIL`, and `CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN` on the backend when no mock source URL is configured; pages are stored as verified `Document` nodes. Jira records route through ticket identification. Some GitHub and Slack records route through feature-update processing. Other sources use the backend `MOCK_API_BASE_URL`. Credentials are not accepted in browser requests. The endpoint returns counts and outcomes, not raw source content or a persistent execution trace. The frontend shows returned outcomes and links processed graph entity IDs.

metadata.title: Backend API capability inventory

documentation:docs%2Fapi-capability-inve.text:
[LangGraph ingestion behavior]

ounts and outcomes, not raw source content or a persistent execution trace. The frontend shows returned outcomes and links processed graph entity IDs.

The assistant query endpoint `POST /api/assistant/query` runs a LangGraph workflow: validate, classify, retrieve graph entities and direct neighbors, optionally synthesize with the configured model, and validate a structured response. With model configuration disabled or unavailable, it returns deterministic summaries, verified graph citations, uncertainty, and execution stage statuses. It supports company overview, entity lookup, ownership lookup, decision investigation, impact traversal, graph query, and general explanation. Impact output explicitly reports direct graph traversal and does not claim a simulation. The response renderer uses an allowlist of predefined React views, and citation links resolve to graph-backed entities or their indexed source URL.

metadata.title: Backend API capability inventory

documentation:docs%2Fapi-capability-inve.text:
[LangGraph ingestion behavior]

n. The response renderer uses an allowlist of predefined React views, and citation links resolve to graph-backed entities or their indexed source URL.

Assistant memory is stored in FalkorDB as conversation-scoped episodic turns and workspace-scoped semantic entity references and procedural execution stages. Memory is used for follow-up context, not as factual evidence. The API currently scopes this data using a hash of the `x-orgmind-user-id` email header. This is suitable only for the current demo login: the backend has no authentication middleware, so clients can spoof that identity. Deployments with real users must bind the owner identity to a verified server-side session/JWT before treating it as a security boundary.

metadata.title: Backend API capability inventory

documentation:docs%2Fapi-capability-inve.text:
## Capabilities not exposed

There is no separate source-citation retrieval endpoint, authenticated Jira/GitHub/Slack connector, dedicated decision-history service, causal investigation service, impact simulation, proactive insight API, or detailed agent tool-trace API. Indexed source records are retrievable through graph search and neighborhoods. The assistant distinguishes recorded relationships from inferred impact and does not claim to simulate impact. Rich renderers for conflicting-document comparisons, missing-approval audits, task proposals, proactive insights, and multi-stage tool traces are not yet exposed by the current backend response contract.

documentation:README.md:0.text:
# OrgInGraphs

OrgInGraphs is an AI-powered company knowledge graph project. The backend provides a deterministic synthetic Hirenova company graph, FalkorDB persistence through openCypher, REST APIs for exploring company records, and a LangGraph workflow for mock-source ingestion.

metadata.title: OrgInGraphs

documentation:README.md:1.text:
## Project details

- **Version:** 1.0.0
- **Authors:** Garima,Nikhil and Mohit
- **Runtime:** Node.js
- **Language:** TypeScript
- **Package manager:** npm

metadata.title: OrgInGraphs

documentation:README.md:2.text:
## Current status

The backend serves synthetic company data and includes an opt-in LangGraph ingestion workflow for configured mock Jira, Confluence, GitHub, and Slack APIs. It does not provide authenticated third-party connectors. Seed records identify their source system and reserved example URLs.

metadata.title: OrgInGraphs

documentation:README.md:3.text:
## Prerequisites

- Node.js 20 or newer
- npm
- A reachable FalkorDB Cloud graph for `seed:falkordb` and the API

metadata.title: OrgInGraphs

documentation:README.md:4.text:
## Backend installation

```bash
cd backend
npm install
cp .env.example .env
```

The `.env.example` file contains application settings and placeholder FalkorDB connection variables. Update the values for local development as needed. Do not commit `.env` or real secrets.

Relevant variables are `PORT`, `NODE_ENV`, `COMPANY_START_DATE` (ISO date; Hirenova is founded exactly three years earlier), `FALKORDB_HOST`, `FALKORDB_PORT`, `FALKORDB_USERNAME`, `FALKORDB_PASSWORD`, `FALKORDB_TLS`, and `FALKORDB_DATABASE`. The API allows browser requests from `http://localhost:3000` and `http://127.0.0.1:3000` by default; set `FRONTEND_ORIGINS` to a comma-separated origin list to override those defaults.

metadata.title: OrgInGraphs

documentation:README.md:5.text:
[Backend installation]

om `http://localhost:3000` and `http://127.0.0.1:3000` by default; set `FRONTEND_ORIGINS` to a comma-separated origin list to override those defaults.

LLM processing is optional. Leave `MODEL_PROVIDER=disabled` for deterministic evidence-based answers and offline document processing. To enable Gemini synthesis, set `MODEL_PROVIDER=gemini` and `GEMINI_API_KEY`; `GEMINI_MODEL` defaults to `gemini-2.5-flash`. Alternatively, the existing `openai-compatible` provider accepts `MODEL_BASE_URL`, `MODEL_API_KEY`, and `MODEL_DEFAULT_ID`. Optionally override `MODEL_TICKET_ID`, `MODEL_FEATURE_UPDATE_ID`, and their temperatures. `MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS` controls request timeout. Credentials are read only from the backend environment and sent from the backend to the model provider; they are never exposed to browser code or written to graph records. `POST /api/assistant/query` runs the LangGraph retrieval and structured response workflow. Assistant conversation routes persist conversation turns and memory in FalkorDB, scoped by the current demo workspace identity. Confluence can be fetched with backend-only `CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL`, `CONFLUENCE_EMAIL`, and `CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN`; Jira/GitHub/Slack ingestion uses `MOCK_API_BASE_URL`.

metadata.title: OrgInGraphs

documentation:README.md:6.text:
## Available commands

Run these commands from the `backend/` directory:

```bash
npm run dev      # Start the TypeScript entry point in watch mode
npm run build    # Compile TypeScript into dist/
npm start        # Run the compiled application
npm test         # Run seed integrity tests
npm run seed:generate  # Write deterministic seed-data.json
npm run seed:validate  # Validate without database access
npm run seed:falkordb  # MERGE the seed into configured FalkorDB
```

metadata.title: OrgInGraphs

documentation:README.md:7.text:
## Backend API

After `npm run seed:falkordb` and `npm run dev`, the following endpoints are available:

- `GET /health`
- `GET /api/graph`
- `GET /api/company`
- `GET /api/employees?departmentId=swe&teamId=eng&employmentStatus=active`
- `GET /api/employees/:employeeId`
- `GET /api/departments` and `GET /api/departments/:departmentId`
- `GET /api/projects` and `GET /api/projects/:projectId`
- `GET /api/graph/neighborhood/Employee/emp-03`
- `GET /api/search?q=idempotency`
- `GET /api/product-progress/graph`
- `POST /api/ingestion/process` with `{ "source": "jira", "limit": 20 }`

`GET /api/graph` returns the complete graph in one request:

metadata.title: OrgInGraphs
OrgInGraphs

documentation:README.md:9.text:
[Backend API]

ng the result.

Invalid IDs, filters, entity types, and empty search terms return `400`; missing records return `404`; database failures return `503`.

The neighborhood response includes each node's `entityType` and each edge's actual `from`, `to`, and `direction` (`incoming` or `outgoing`) so graph clients can render the relationship accurately.

The ingestion endpoint returns a status, fetched-record count, per-record outcomes, unresolved references, and safe errors. `docs/api-capability-inventory.md` maps the current API capabilities and limitations to frontend components.

metadata.title: OrgInGraphs

documentation:README.md:10.text:
## Frontend

The Next.js frontend is in `frontend/`. See [frontend/README.md](frontend/README.md) for installation, environment configuration, and development commands. Run the frontend on port `3000` and the backend on port `8080`.

metadata.title: OrgInGraphs

documentation:README.md:11.text:
## Project structure

```text
OrgInGraphs/
├── backend/
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── api/       # Express read endpoints and validation
│   │   ├── config/    # Environment loading and validation
│   │   ├── db/        # FalkorDB client and idempotent graph writes
│   │   ├── seed/      # Deterministic generation and validation
│   │   └── types/     # Shared TypeScript types
│   ├── scripts/       # Seed commands
│   ├── tests/         # Seed integrity tests
│   ├── .env.example
│   ├── .gitignore
│   ├── package.json
│   └── tsconfig.json
├── frontend/         # Next.js organizational graph and workspace UI
└── README.md
```

metadata.title: OrgInGraphs
